item.title: DisciplinaJudicialAI
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Conversational assistant that guides judicial servants on the disciplinary regime (Laws 1952 of 2019, 2094 of 2021 and 270 of 1996), without advice on specific cases.
Status Published, with a public demo.
Scope General guidance. It does not replace advice from a lawyer and does not handle specific cases.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2025 Daniel”.
Code HammerDev99/disciplinajudicialai
Demo disciplinajudicialai.streamlit.app (in Spanish). The demo uses third-party AI services. Do not enter personal data or information from real cases.
Started First commit: 6 March 2026.
Recognition None.
Authorship Built by the author from a template by another author (template author’s profile), with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Explains the stages and deadlines of the disciplinary process.
  • Guides users on how offences are classified, the sanctions and the rights of the person under investigation.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit, the OpenAI Assistants API and the texts of the cited laws.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.

item.title: TutelaBot (adaptation)
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Conversational assistant on the acción de tutela (constitutional protection action) and the right of petition, based on the 1991 Constitution, Decree 2591 of 1991 and Law 1755 of 2015.
Status Published (adaptation), with a public demo.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2023” held by the author of the original project.
Code HammerDev99/TutelaBot
Demo tutela-bot.streamlit.app (in Spanish). The demo uses third-party AI services. Do not enter personal data or information from real cases.
Started Adaptation since 18 September 2025.
Recognition None.
Authorship Adaptation of an MIT-licensed project by another author. Changes by the author (September and October 2025): own assistant configuration, reference legal documents, removal of one module, and usage analytics. Done with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Explains the requirements, procedure and deadlines of the acción de tutela.
  • Guides users on exercising the right of petition before public and private entities.
  • Answers in plain language, citing the relevant legal provisions.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit and the OpenAI Assistants API.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.

item.title: LLM Chat App
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Streamlit chat interface for talking to Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI (GPT) models through their APIs, with deployment scripts for Ubuntu.
Status Published.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2025 Daniel Arbeláez Álvarez”.
Code HammerDev99/BotApiClaude
Started First commit: 3 July 2025.
Recognition None.
Authorship Personal project of the author, developed with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Lets the user pick a provider and model and chat with history.
  • The API key is entered by the person using the app.
  • Includes a Dockerfile and deployment scripts with Caddy and systemd.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit, Docker, Caddy and systemd.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.
